entries.real_world_scenario:
We can point to other such forces that emerged from this deep past and
that similarly mold our everyday behavior-for instance, our need to
continually rank ourselves and measure our self-worth through our status is
a trait that is noticeable among all hunter-gatherer cultures, and even among
chimpanzees, as are our tribal instincts, which cause us to divide people
into insiders or outsiders.

To imagine that we are not always in control of what we do is a frightening thought, but in fact it is the reality. Look at our anger, for instance.
